data.name: Balough
data.gender_notes: Balough is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Testament name Beloch or Belogos, meaning 'strong warrior'. In the Bible, Beloch is mentioned as a son of Azazel and a prince of demons. Despite this dark origin, the name can be reclaimed and used as a symbol of inner strength and courage. The name Balough carries the meaning “Strong warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Balough usually hope their child will grow to embody strong warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Balough belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balough total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Balough may have once carried negative connotations due to its dark origins in the Old Testament, being associated with Beloch, a prince of demons. However, as a unique and intriguing name, it can now be reclaimed and used as a source of inspiration, particularly for those who value strength and courage in their daily lives. The name carries an air of mystery and intrigue, which can be appealing to those looking for a name that stands out from the crowd.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Balough holds spiritual significance as a reminder of inner strength and courage, even when faced with challenges or adversity. Despite its dark origins, the name can be seen as a symbol of power and resilience, inspiring those who bear it to overcome obstacles and face the world with confidence and determination. Further, for those with a deep spiritual connection to the Bible, the name may hold additional significance as a reminder of their faith and the strength that comes from it.
